comment: Ellastic Net — Oldies but goodies: Zou, Hastie, Regularization and variable selection via the elastic net, 2005. Interpolates between the Lasso (l1) and Ridge regression (l2). The regularization path of Lasso is polygonal. The one of elastic… https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_net_regularization

title: Graphical Lasso
comment: Graphical Lasso — Conditional independence of entries of Gaussian vectors defines a graph associated to the inverse of the covariance (precision matrix). Graphical Lasso estimates a sparse graph by l^1 penalizing the maximum likelihood estimator. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Graphical_lasso
alt_text: Graphical Lasso. Conditional independence of entries of Gaussian vectors defines a graph associated to the inverse of the covariance (precision matrix). Graphical Lasso estimates a sparse graph by l^1 penalizing the maximum likelihood estimator.

title: Moving Least Squares
comment: Moving Least Squares — Moving least square is a mesh-free interpolation method which performs a localized weighted least square with singular weights. The case of constant polynomial is Shepard's method. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moving_least_squares
alt_text: Moving Least Squares. Moving least square is a mesh-free interpolation method which performs a localized weighted least square with singular weights. The case of constant polynomial is Shepard's method.

comment: Wirtinger — Classic reference: Wilhelm Wirtinger, Zur formalen Theorie der Funktionen von mehr komplexen Veränderlichen, 1926. Wirtinger derivatives treat complex valued functions of complex variables as if they were real functions. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wirtinger_derivatives

title: Kernel Ridge
comment: Kernel Ridge — Kernel ridge regression approximates a function using a sum of kernel functions. The kernel must be symmetric positive semi-definite, for instance Gaussian or Laplacian. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kernel_method

title: Hermite
comment: Hermite — Hermite functions form an ortho-basis of the continuous Fourier transform. Coming up with their discrete counterpart (discrete eigenvectors of the FFT) is surprisingly hard and apparently still mostly an open problem. https://arxiv.org/pdf/1501.07646.pdf

title: Ica

title: Zeta
